metadata.setting_description:
The tavern is a rectangular space thirty feet wide from east to west and twenty feet deep from north to south. The western wall holds the heavy oak front entrance; the northern wall near its centre contains the back door with a wooden latch. Beneath the floor are creaking oak planks laid in long rows along the east‑west axis, each three inches thick and twelve inches wide.

At the heart of the room stands a ten‑foot‑long central counter that runs adjacent to the hearth built into the north wall; its back edge lies directly against the stone blaze. Inside the hearth’s fire‑box rests a barrel holding ale or beer.

To the east side of the counter sits a single six‑by‑two foot back table, positioned just inside the room’s eastern boundary. Lanterns hang from wrought‑iron sconces at each corner of this table and at intervals along the northern wall, providing steady illumination.

Near the south end of the tavern is a high bar stool resting upon a narrow counter platform four feet long and one foot wide. Above this stool extends a shelf that holds crystal cups in a neat row; the shelf stretches from east to west across the back of the stool just above floor level.

All objects are spaced so they do not overlap: the hearth sits at the north wall centre, the counter runs adjacent to it along the eastern side of the room, the back table occupies space near the eastern corner, and the bar stool with crystal cups is positioned in the south‑eastern quadrant. The wooden latch on the back door remains accessible from inside the tavern, allowing easy exit for patrons or staff.
metadata.spatial_location_description:
A heavy oak front door opens onto a rectangular tavern that measures thirty feet wide (east‑west) by twenty feet deep (north‑south).  
The back door sits on the north wall near its centre and has a single wooden latch.

Beneath the floor are creaking oak planks, each three inches thick and twelve inches wide, laid in long rows along the east‑west axis. Their worn surface gives the room an unmistakably medieval feel.

At the heart of the tavern stands a central counter that is ten feet long and three feet deep. The counter’s back edge lies directly against a hearth built into the north wall; the hearth itself is a stone blaze with a barrel resting within its fire‑box, holding barrels of ale or beer.  

To the east side of the counter sits a single back table, six feet wide by two feet deep, positioned just inside the room’s eastern boundary. Lanterns hang from wrought‑iron sconces on each corner of this table and at intervals along the northern wall, providing steady illumination.

Near the south end of the tavern stands a high bar stool that rests upon a narrow counter platform four feet long and one foot wide. Above this stool is a shelf that holds crystal cups in a neat row; the shelf extends from east to west across the back of the stool, just above the floor level.

All objects are spaced so they do not overlap: the hearth sits at the north wall centre, the counter runs adjacent to it along the eastern side of the room, the back table occupies the space near the eastern corner, and the bar stool with crystal cups is positioned in the south‑eastern quadrant. The wooden latch on the back door remains accessible from inside the tavern, allowing easy exit for patrons or staff.
